column1: # words/aliases.tsv -- SECOND SPELLINGS of a word: `spelling<TAB>the word it spells`.
# AN ALIAS HAS NO NUMBER AND NO ROW, which is why it is not in words_004.tsv. A
# word's 16-bit code is 4097 plus its ROW, so a second row for one word would be a
# second code for it -- and the checker, the walker and every table that compares a
# code would then need to be told the two are the same word. Here the lexer turns
# the second spelling into the FIRST word's code, and nothing after the lexer ever
# learns there were two. 003 did the same with SAT_ALIAS in words.def.
# make_word_codes.py reads this file and refuses a row whose spelling is already a
# word, or whose word is not one: a typo here would otherwise lex as nothing at all.
# THE AUTHOR, 2026-09-22: "namespace will be namespace/space, and class will be
# spacesuit alias class, so a class remains a spacesuit and that is my final
# answer". satellite.namespace and satellite.spacesuit are the words; these are
# the second spellings, and a refusal names the word, as 003's did for `class`.
satellite.space
satellite.class
# THE AUTHOR, 2026-09-22, naming five types at once as "real_name/alias":
# "satellite.variable.float/double, satellite.variable.binary/bin
# satellite.variable.hex/hexadecimal satellite.variable.percent/percentage". He
# wrote percent first there, but percentage is the word 004 already has
# (1 6 16, 2026-09-17), so percent is its second spelling. The colour is spelled
# `color` every time he writes it; `colour` is how a window piece's method is
# spelled (`.colour("#rrggbb")`), so either spelling reaches the one word.
satellite.variable.double
satellite.variable.bin
satellite.variable.hexadecimal
satellite.variable.percent
satellite.variable.colour
